scenario.prompt_to_agent:
PC users report no noticeable problems with internal traffic.
Internet access also works. But network monitoring shows R1's
ECMP path count dropped from 2 to 1 and all internet traffic
now takes a single path through CSW2 only. CSW1 reports an
OSPF neighbor went down. What changed?

injection.action: shut down the link to r1

post_inject_check.command: ip -br link show eth0 | grep -c UP

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: csw1 eth0 / link CSW1 <-> R1 (10.0.0.32/30)
Mechanism: r1 has two ECMP-eligible paths to the OSPF backbone
  via CSW1 (10.0.0.33) and CSW2 (10.0.0.37). With CSW1's eth0
  down, the adjacency drops and the CSW1-side path is removed.
  All traffic falls onto the CSW2 path; capacity is halved
  but no outage because OSPF converges.
Localization: csw1 (eth0)
Root cause: physical/logical link between CSW1 and R1 is down
Fix: `ip link set eth0 up` on csw1 (or investigate cabling if
  in real hardware)
scenario.fix_spec:
`ip link set eth0 up` on csw1 (or investigate cabling if
  in real hardware)

line.command: ip -br link show eth0 | grep -c UP

agent.diagnosis_text:
The fault is a kernel-level administrative shutdown of csw1's eth0 interface
(10.0.0.34/30, connected to r1 via collision domain CD_WAN_LINK_1). Someone
issued "ip link set eth0 down" on csw1 — the interface shows state DOWN with
no UP or RUNNING flags in the kernel, yet the FRR running configuration is
intact and correctly advertises network 10.0.0.32/30 area 0 with no shutdown
statement. Because the L2 carrier is gone, FRR's Zebra immediately marked
eth0 as operationally down and disabled OSPF on it ("eth0 is down — OSPF not
enabled on this interface").

As a result, csw1 lost its OSPF adjacency with r1 and stopped both receiving
and advertising LSAs over that link. From r1's perspective, the hello timer
on eth0 expired (dead timer was already at ~17 s when first observed), dropping
the adjacency to csw1 (router-ID 10.0.0.77) entirely. R1's routing table now
forwards every OSPF-learned internal prefix exclusively via eth1 → 10.0.0.38
(csw2), weight 1 — no ECMP. All internet-bound traffic from internal hosts
therefore traverses only the csw2 → r1 WAN path.

Root cause: csw1's eth0 was brought down at the OS layer, tearing the
OSPF adjacency with r1 and eliminating one of the two ECMP WAN uplinks.

Corrective fix: On csw1, run "ip link set eth0 up". The interface already has
its IP address (10.0.0.34/30) and FRR OSPF configuration intact, so the OSPF
adjacency with r1 will re-form immediately and ECMP will be restored within
one OSPF hello interval (~10 s).

per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly identifies csw1's eth0 link to R1 (the CSW1<->R1 WAN link) as the affected link.
The report explicitly names csw1's eth0 and states the interface is DOWN (admin shutdown / no RUNNING flag), satisfying the component and link-state requirement.
The report explicitly identifies two ECMP-capable WAN uplinks and explains that with csw1's eth0 down all traffic shifted to the csw2 path (no ECMP), matching the redundant-path failure pattern.
Bringing csw1's eth0 back up (ip link set eth0 up) restores the L2 carrier so FRR/Zebra will re-enable OSPF and the adjacency to r1 will reform, restoring ECMP.

The investigation log clearly shows csw1's eth0 is DOWN at the OS level and that the OSPF adjacency to r1 was lost; the agent's inference that this removed one ECMP path and shifted traffic to the remaining path is a reasonable causal conclusion though explicit routing-table/ECMP output is not shown. Evidence is sufficient to localize the failure to csw1 eth0 and to recommend ip link set eth0 up.
